headline: Contained overnight NQ rotation keeps Tail low; 24-year-high long yields keep Stress high into quarter-end data cluster
body: NQ futures trade near 30,650, about 0.1% firmer, inside a contained overnight band of roughly 30,571-30,737 with price mid-range rather than held at an extreme. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed September 29 at 30,339.33, up 0.21%, after a narrow 30,235.67-30,429.97 session range, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped 0.09%, the S&P 500 fell 0.16% and the Dow lost 0.26%. Retracements have been present in both cash and futures and the VIX sits near 16.04, so there is no observed evidence of persistent one-way structure or repeated extension after failed pullbacks; Tail therefore stays in the low band. The Stress backdrop is genuinely difficult: the 30-year Treasury yield reached 5.62% on September 29, its highest since 2002, the 10-year printed 5.28% intraday and holds near 5.24%, its highest area since 2007, and Federal Reserve commentary points to a hiking rather than easing bias, with the New York Fed president indicating the central bank could wait until December before raising rates again. Conference Board consumer confidence fell to 81.9 from 88.6 against an 89 expectation, a more-than-12-year low, and August JOLTS openings came in at 7.097 million versus 7.228 million expected. WTI crude near $89.48 and Brent near $96.21 remain elevated but eased in the prior session on improving Middle East energy flows and a further US emergency reserve release, so oil is currently a de-escalating input. Megacap behaviour is dispersed rather than aligned: Apple fell 2.66% to $329.40 on management-restructuring reports and an AI competitive flag, while Meta rose 3.24% and Arm gained 3.65%, with Nvidia down 0.72%. That internal dispersion argues against index-level directional efficiency. September 30 is the final session of Q3, so rebalancing flow overlays a dense release cluster: ADP at 12:15Z, August PCE and core PCE together with the Q2 GDP final estimate at 12:30Z, Chicago PMI at 13:45Z and EIA crude stocks at 14:30Z. The principal conditional path to mean-reversion failure is a firm core PCE print driving a fresh long-end yield extension that compresses long-duration technology valuations without meaningful retracement; that path is a scenario rather than an observation. The shared Finviz context file was read at the start of this run and was both stale, generated 2026-09-29T23:14:22Z, and partial, with its futures and calendar sections unavailable, so it was not used as current evidence and full independent research was performed instead.

lookbackSummary: Across the 24 hours to 03:00Z, published Claude assessments eased steadily from Tail 24 with Stress 79 in the early hours of September 29 to Tail 16 with Stress 65 by the final slot. The September 29 US session produced a narrow Nasdaq-100 range and a mid-range close despite the 30-year yield reaching a 24-year high, and dominant mode migrated from trend-down through mixed to normal as two-sided behaviour reasserted itself. One hour, 14:00Z on September 29, has no published assessment and remains explicitly unavailable.
outlookSummary: The horizon is shaped by one dense catalyst cluster on the final session of Q3. Conditional Tail stays in the low band through the Asian and European hours, lifts to the watch band across 13:00Z-15:00Z as August PCE, the Q2 GDP final estimate, the US cash open and Chicago PMI overlap, then decays through the US afternoon. Stress rises into the release window and again into the 20:00Z quarter-end closing auction before easing overnight. No slot reaches the block threshold on current evidence; the identified invalidation is a post-release long-end yield extension that produces shallow pullbacks and repeated extension in the index.
